topics.topic: Precedence between resource exhaustion and cleanup failure in execute_function results
questions: If an oversized output or a MemoryError during output handling is followed by an unconfirmed reap or exchange-directory removal, must the result remain resource_exhausted and never crashed, or must cleanup_failed override it with crashed?

quotes: a MemoryError while it pre-counts, encodes or sends the outputs is a memory hit too, so an output too large to send concludes resource_exhausted, never crashed.
when either cannot be confirmed the outputs are discarded and the result is outcome crashed with detail_code cleanup_failed of = models.DetailCode;
judgement.divergence: One implementation preserves resource_exhausted after an output-memory hit despite cleanup failure; another overrides it with crashed and cleanup_failed, which the caller notices in SandboxResult.
judgement.why: The unconditional cleanup-failure result conflicts with the statement that an output too large to send is resource_exhausted and never crashed.

topics.topic: Timing of UTF-8 encoding during execute_function output pre-counting
questions: Must the runner encode each value to UTF-8 while pre-counting it, or must all encoding occur only after pre-counting?

quotes: Before that, the runner, given bounds.output_bytes in its configuration and having no canonical_bytes inside the environment, pre-counts the returned outputs before it encodes or sends any — each value output as the UTF-8 bytes of json.dumps with sort_keys=True, separators (',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False and allow_nan=False, each file output as its bytes — and when that pre-count exceeds the bound it sends no output and reports a resource hit;
judgement.divergence: One implementation UTF-8-encodes value JSON during pre-counting; another postpones UTF-8 encoding until after pre-counting, which can change when MemoryError is observed and therefore the SandboxResult seen by the caller.
judgement.why: The passage says pre-counting occurs before encoding while also requiring each value to be pre-counted as UTF-8 bytes.
judgement.failure: a contradiction needs two quotes found verbatim in the texts

topics.topic: Whether an oversized mapped output with no element failure record makes the node failed and how the failure derivation must reflect that
questions: Must the definition of failed include an oversized mapped-node aggregate with no failing element record, or must that aggregate no longer make the node failed?
How can the mapped node count as failed by this derivation when it has no NodeExecution or ElementFailed record, or which passage must change?

Must an oversized mapped value list count as a failed node despite having no failed function-element NodeExecution or failed operation-element conclusion, or must the definition of failed be expanded?
Must the no-record oversized-list condition be added to the failed derivation, or must it stop counting as failed?

quotes: when its canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant nothing is written and the node is failed for its dependants, which conclude upstream_failed, every element record staying as it is;

failed means a function element whose NodeExecution status is contract_violation, sandbox_violation, timeout, resource_exhausted or crashed, and an operation element that operation_element_conclusion answers ElementFailed, whatever that conclusion's status (operation_refused, operation_failed, or outcome_unknown for applied_outputs_unknown);

if nothing waits, the run ends succeeded when every node concluded succeeded or skipped_by_guard and failed otherwise, a mapped node whose delivered value list is over the stored value ceiling counting as failed by the same derivation, with no record of its own, with ended_at set and no waiting points.
judgement.why: The texts require an oversized mapped aggregate with no record to count as failed, while defining failure only through a failed function-element NodeExecution or operation-element ElementFailed conclusion.
